description: Focaccia Genovese is a true masterpiece of Ligurian baking, celebrated for its wonderfully chewy interior and irresistibly crisp, salty crust. Infused with aromatic rosemary and the finest olive oil, this traditional flatbread is perfect for dipping, sandwiches, or simply enjoyed on its own. Experience a taste of Genoa with every delightful bite of this rustic Italian classic.

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the warm water, sugar, and active dry yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active. This is crucial for a good rise.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: Add the flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Drizzle in 1/4 cup of the extra virgin olive oil and continue to mix until it's mostly incorporated. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic. It should be slightly tacky.

instructions.title: First Rise
instructions.text: Lightly grease a clean bowl with olive oil. Place the dough in the bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size. This slow rise develops flavor.

instructions.title: Shape and Dimple
instructions.text: Gently punch down the dough and transfer it to a 9x13 inch baking pan generously drizzled with 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Press the dough evenly into the pan. Using your fingertips, create deep dimples all over the surface of the focaccia. Drizzle generously with more olive oil.

instructions.title: Second Rise and Toppings
instructions.text: Cover the pan again with plastic wrap or a kitchen towel and let the focaccia rise for another 30-45 minutes in a warm place, or until puffy. Preheat your oven to 425F (220C). Once risen, sprinkle the surface with chopped fresh rosemary and flaky sea salt.

instructions.title: Bake to Perfection
instructions.text: Bake the focaccia in the preheated oven for 20-30 minutes, or until golden brown on top and cooked through. The bottom should also be nicely browned. If it browns too quickly, you can loosely tent it with foil.

instructions.title: Cool and Serve
instructions.text: Once baked, immediately remove the focaccia from the pan and place it on a wire rack to cool slightly. Drizzle with a final touch of fresh extra virgin olive oil before slicing and serving warm. Enjoy the authentic taste of Genoa!

tips: For the best texture, use a high-quality bread flour if available, as its higher protein content develops stronger gluten for that characteristic chew.
Do not skimp on the olive oil. A generous amount both in the dough and on top is essential for the authentic taste and crispy crust of Focaccia Genovese.
Serve focaccia warm, either on its own, with a good quality balsamic vinegar and olive oil for dipping, or as a side to soups and salads. It also makes excellent sandwiches.
article:
Discover the culinary heart of Liguria with Focaccia Genovese, a true masterpiece of Italian baking. More than just a simple flatbread, this iconic delicacy from Genoa embodies centuries of tradition, characterized by its irresistibly airy crumb, crisp exterior, and a generous sheen of golden olive oil. While many focaccias exist, the Genovese style stands apart, offering a unique texture and flavor profile that makes it a beloved staple in Italy and across the globe. When infused with fragrant rosemary, it transforms into an aromatic delight, perfect for any time of day. Prepare to embark on a delicious journey into the world of authentic Italian baking, where quality ingredients and a touch of patience yield extraordinary results.

## What is Focaccia Genovese?
Focaccia Genovese is the quintessential focaccia, originating from Genoa in the Liguria region of Italy. Unlike its thicker, often bread-like cousins from other regions, the Genovese version is distinctly thin, incredibly light, and exceptionally airy, with a characteristic chewy interior and a delightfully crisp crust. Its surface is famously dimpled, creating perfect little pools for the extra virgin olive oil and coarse sea salt that are applied before baking. The high hydration dough and specific proofing techniques contribute to its unique structure, making it incredibly tender and almost melt-in-your-mouth. Historically, it was a baker's breakfast, often dipped in coffee or wine, but today it's enjoyed throughout the day, either plain, as an accompaniment to meals, or as a base for sandwiches. The essence of authentic Focaccia Genovese lies in its simplicity and the quality of its core ingredients.

## Ingredients for Rosemary Olive Oil Focaccia
Crafting the perfect Rosemary Olive Oil Focaccia Genovese requires a few high-quality ingredients.
*   **Strong Bread Flour:** A high-protein flour is essential for developing the gluten structure needed for that characteristic chewy, airy texture. Italian "Tipo 0" or "Tipo 00" flour can be used, but a good quality bread flour will also work wonders.
*   **Water:** Hydration is key. The dough will be quite wet, contributing to the focaccia's lightness.
*   **Fresh Yeast:** Active dry yeast or instant yeast will both work. Fresh yeast often imparts a slightly better flavor.
*   **Extra Virgin Olive Oil:** This is non-negotiable. A high-quality, fruity extra virgin olive oil not only adds incredible flavor but also contributes to the focaccia's tender crumb and golden crust. Don't skimp here!
*   **Sea Salt:** Coarse sea salt for sprinkling on top provides a delightful textural contrast and bursts of briny flavor. Fine salt for the dough.
*   **Fresh Rosemary:** Stripped from its woody stems and roughly chopped, fresh rosemary infuses the focaccia with its signature fragrant, slightly piney aroma and taste.

## How to Make Authentic Focaccia Genovese: Step-by-Step
Making Focaccia Genovese is a rewarding process that requires patience but is surprisingly simple.

1.  **Activate the Yeast:** In a large bowl, dissolve the fresh yeast in warm water (around 105-115°F or 40-46°C) with a pinch of sugar. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
2.  **Mix the Dough:** Add the flour, a generous drizzle of olive oil, and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Mix with a wooden spoon or in a stand mixer with a dough hook until a shaggy dough forms. The dough will be very wet and sticky – resist the urge to add more flour.
3.  **Kneading (Minimal):** Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface or keep it in the mixer. Knead for about 5-7 minutes until it becomes somewhat smoother and more elastic. For a no-knead approach, you can perform several "stretch and fold" cycles over a few hours.
4.  **First Proof:** Drizzle a clean bowl with olive oil and transfer the dough to it, turning to coat. Cover with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until doubled in size.
5.  **Prepare the Pan:** Liberally coat a large baking sheet (approximately 13x18 inches or 33x45 cm) with extra virgin olive oil.
6.  **Transfer and Stretch:** Gently transfer the risen dough to the prepared baking sheet. Using your oiled fingertips, gently press and stretch the dough to fill the pan. It's okay if it resists; let it rest for 10-15 minutes, then continue stretching.
7.  **Second Proof & Dimpling:** Once the dough fills the pan, cover it again and let it rise for another 30-45 minutes. Then, using your oiled fingertips, create deep dimples across the entire surface of the Focaccia Genovese. Don't be shy – these dimples are crucial for its texture.
8.  **Flavoring:** In a small bowl, whisk together a few tablespoons of olive oil with a tablespoon of water and a pinch of salt. Pour this mixture over the dimpled dough. Sprinkle generously with fresh rosemary and coarse sea salt.
9.  **Bake:** Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C). Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the Focaccia Genovese is golden brown and cooked through.
10. **Cool and Serve:** Transfer the focaccia to a wire rack to cool slightly. Slice and serve warm.

## Tips for the Perfect Genovese Focaccia
Achieving that authentic, airy Focaccia Genovese requires attention to a few key details:

*   **Hydration is Key:** Don't be afraid of a wet, sticky dough. It's what gives the focaccia its characteristic open crumb. Resist adding too much extra flour during mixing or kneading.
*   **Quality Olive Oil:** This cannot be stressed enough. A good quality extra virgin olive oil is integral to the flavor and texture, both in the dough and as a topping.
*   **Proper Proofing:** Allow ample time for the dough to rise. Under-proofed dough will be dense, while over-proofed dough can collapse. Look for a visibly doubled size and a springy texture when gently poked.
*   **Deep Dimples:** Really press your fingers into the dough to create those signature dimples. They trap the olive oil and create pockets of air, contributing to the focaccia's unique texture.
*   **Oven Temperature:** A hot oven is crucial for a good crust and quick rise. Ensure your oven is fully preheated before baking.
*   **Don't Overbake:** Keep an eye on the focaccia. It should be golden brown, not dark brown, to retain its tenderness.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings
Rosemary Olive Oil Focaccia Genovese is incredibly versatile. Enjoy it simply on its own, perhaps with a glass of good Italian wine, for a truly authentic experience. It makes a fantastic accompaniment to a variety of dishes:
*   **Antipasto Platter:** Serve alongside cured meats, cheeses, marinated olives, and roasted vegetables.
*   **Soups and Salads:** Perfect for dipping into a hearty minestrone or alongside a fresh caprese salad.
*   **Sandwiches:** Its sturdy yet tender crumb makes it an excellent choice for a gourmet sandwich base.
*   **Breakfast or Snack:** A traditional way to enjoy it in Liguria is for breakfast, sometimes dipped in coffee or milk. It's also a wonderful mid-afternoon snack.
*   **With Dips:** Pair with balsamic vinegar and olive oil, pesto, or a flavorful hummus.

## Variations and Substitutions for Focaccia
While the classic Rosemary Olive Oil Focaccia Genovese is perfect as is, there are many ways to adapt focaccia to your taste:

*   **Other Herbs:** While rosemary is traditional for this specific focaccia, you can experiment with fresh thyme, oregano, or a mix of Italian herbs.
*   **Garlic:** Add thinly sliced fresh garlic or garlic powder to the olive oil topping for an extra aromatic kick.
*   **Onions:** Caramelized onions or thinly sliced red onions can be pressed into the dough before baking for a savory twist.
*   **Tomatoes:** Halved cherry tomatoes or sun-dried tomatoes are popular additions, providing bursts of juicy sweetness.
*   **Olives:** Kalamata or green olives, pitted and sliced, can be scattered over the top.
*   **Cheese:** A sprinkling of Parmesan or mozzarella towards the end of baking can add a cheesy layer.
*   **Flour Blends:** While strong bread flour is best for the classic texture, you can experiment with a small percentage of whole wheat flour for added nuttiness and fiber, though it will alter the lightness.

Embrace the joy of Italian baking by bringing the authentic taste of Focaccia Genovese into your home. This simple yet profound bread, with its perfect balance of crispness, chewiness, and aromatic rosemary-infused olive oil, is more than just food – it's a celebration of tradition, quality ingredients, and the pleasure of sharing. Enjoy every delicious bite!
